rows.question: Is there an income limit above which we get no Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes. Under the federal Elterngeld (parental allowance) law, the entitlement lapses above a set level of zu versteuerndes Einkommen (taxable income).

The rule in the statute:
- For one entitled person, the claim lapses if that person had taxable income of more than 175,000 euros in the last completed tax assessment period before the birth ("im letzten abgeschlossenen Veranlagungszeitraum vor der Geburt des Kindes ein zu versteuerndes Einkommen ... in Höhe von mehr als 175 000 Euro").
- If another person also meets the conditions, for example the other parent living in the same household with the child, the claim lapses if the two incomes added together are more than 175,000 euros ("wenn die Summe des zu versteuernden Einkommens beider Personen mehr als 175 000 Euro beträgt").

The limit refers to taxable income, not gross income. The official family portal explains that taxable income is usually considerably lower than gross income, because certain expenses and allowances are deducted. It also says that taxable income is determined by the Finanzamt and shown in your tax assessment notice.

If the tax assessment notice for that period is not yet available when you apply, the law still allows an application. Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation if the limit turns out to be exceeded after all, or the amount is decided provisionally if it is not yet possible to say whether the limit is exceeded.

The official family portal says that higher limits applied to births before 1 April 2025. The transitional provisions of the statute are not among the sources available here, so this answer gives only the 175,000 euro figure the statute states.

Whether the limit applies to your family, and which rule governs a particular birth, is decided by the Elterngeldstelle for your district. In Hessen, that is the authority to approach.

rows.question: What is Mutterschaftsgeld and when do I apply for it?
rows.reply:
Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay from the health insurer) is a payment for the protection periods before and after the birth and for the day of the birth itself ('für die Zeit der Schutzfristen vor und nach der Entbindung sowie für den Entbindungstag').

Who pays depends on how you are insured:

- Members of a statutory health insurance fund ('Mitglied einer gesetzlichen Krankenkasse') receive Mutterschaftsgeld under the rules of the Social Code, Book V. Under those rules it goes to female members who are entitled to sickness benefit when unable to work, or who are not paid wages because of the maternity protection periods. It also goes to women whose employment ends immediately before the protection period begins, if they were members of a health insurance fund on the last day of employment.
- For members in employment at the start of the protection period, Mutterschaftsgeld is based on average net daily pay over the last three settled calendar months, but is at most 13 euros per calendar day ('höchstens 13 Euro für den Kalendertag'). Any amount above that is paid by the employer, or by the body responsible for paying Mutterschaftsgeld, as an employer supplement ('Zuschuss zum Mutterschaftsgeld').
- Women who are not members of a statutory health insurance fund receive Mutterschaftsgeld paid by the federal government, capped at 210 euros in total ('insgesamt höchstens 210 Euro'). It is paid on application by the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung ('auf Antrag vom Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung').

The Familienportal explains that the protection periods normally begin 6 weeks before the calculated due date and end 8 weeks after the birth.

When to apply: the excerpts do not give a time for applying. They say only that, for payment before the birth, a certificate from a doctor or midwife stating the expected date of delivery is decisive ('das Zeugnis eines Arztes oder einer Hebamme maßgebend, in dem der voraussichtliche Tag der Entbindung angegeben ist').

If you are in statutory health insurance, your health insurance fund is the body to ask about timing. If you are not, the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung is the authority named in the law.

Whether you qualify and how much you would receive is decided by that body, not here.

Mutterschaftsgeld also affects Elterngeld. Statutory Mutterschaftsgeld and the employer supplement for the time from the child's birth are counted against Elterngeld. The 210-euro payment under § 19 Absatz 2 MuSchG is excluded from this.

rows.question: Can I work while receiving Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes, the law allows it, within a limit. Elterngeld (parental allowance) goes to a person who does no paid work or does not work full time: "keine oder keine volle Erwerbstätigkeit ausübt" (BEEG §1(1) no. 4).

The law says a person is not working full time in any of these three cases (BEEG §1(6)):
1. their working hours do not exceed 32 hours a week, averaged over the child's month of life ("32 Wochenstunden im Durchschnitt des Lebensmonats");
2. they are in employment for vocational training ("Beschäftigung zur Berufsbildung");
3. they work as a suitable childminder within the meaning of §§ 23 and 43 of Book VIII of the Social Code.

Working reduces the payment. The maximum of 1,800 euros a month is paid for full months of life in which you have no earned income (BEEG §2(1)). For months in which you earn less than before the birth, Elterngeld is paid as a percentage of the difference between your earnings before and after the birth. For this, earnings before the birth count up to at most 2,770 euros (BEEG §2(3)).

If your application states that you expect to earn income during the payment period, the amount is first decided provisionally (BEEG §8(3) no. 3). After the payment period ends, you must prove your actual earnings for that time (BEEG §8(1)). Instead of one month of the basic allowance, you can take two months of "Elterngeld Plus" (BEEG §4(3)).

Whether you qualify and how much you would receive is decided only by the Elterngeld office for your district.

the hours limit is stated with its source
